title: Multi-omics single-cell data integration and regulatory inference with graph-linked embedding
training_information: Unpaired assay matrices plus signed, weighted feature-guidance graph; optional additional regulatory evidence.
objective: Modality VAEs, guidance-graph reconstruction and weighted adversarial alignment.
target: Joint cell/feature embeddings and regulatory scores; TF networks additionally combine binding evidence and SCENIC.
training_pairing: Unpaired in core study; extensions can use paired supervision.
validation_information: Paired-cell alignment, paired correlations, pcHi-C/eQTL and curated TF-network evidence.
theorem_applicability: Fixed guidance and identical full assay laws give identical objectives; no general causal-DAG identification theorem found in inspected methods.
positive_restrictions: Shared-state generative model and informative biological feature graph can support regulatory prediction.
evidence_locator: Original Methods: The GLUE framework; Weighted adversarial alignment; Results: Integrative regulatory inference; Discussion.
caveat: Do not dismiss reported regulatory validation; symmetric feature scores alone do not determine causal direction.

title: scConfluence: single-cell diagonal integration with regularized Inverse Optimal Transport on weakly connected features
training_information: Separate matrices and annotations converting some features to a common space; batch labels when available.
objective: Stochastic autoencoder reconstruction, partial-cost-plan inverse OT and latent unbalanced Sinkhorn.
target: Biological cell alignment, clustering and feature imputation.
training_pairing: No cell pairs required.
validation_information: Cell labels and pairing used in evaluation; original task embeds the supplied dataset.
theorem_applicability: The rIOT lemma rewrites an optimization objective for a given plan; it does not identify a biological causal graph.
positive_restrictions: Informative connected features and partial population overlap guide matching.
evidence_locator: Methods: scConfluence, Eqs.7–13; Training details; Outputs.
caveat: Paper squared IOT distance differs from pinned native Euclidean distance; local pilot also changes inputs/evaluation.

title: scMRDR: A Scalable and Flexible Framework for Unpaired Single-Cell Multi-Omics Data Integration
version: NeurIPS 2025 proceedings; inspected author manuscript arXiv v2, 2026-01-17
training_information: Unpaired gene-aligned matrices, activity conversion, feature masks and optional batch covariates; no cell-type labels.
objective: Shared/specific beta-VAE, masked ZINB reconstruction, adversarial modality loss and within-assay isometry.
target: Cell-type conservation, modality/batch mixing, spatial imputation.
training_pairing: No pairs required; shared feature semantics remain an input.
validation_information: Annotated public benchmarks and scIB metrics; labels excluded from training.
theorem_applicability: Section 2 explicitly acknowledges latent nonidentifiability; no causal-identification theorem found in inspected methods.
positive_restrictions: Independent shared/specific latent subspaces and gene-level measurement model with geometry regularization.
caveat: 'No prior' does not mean no gene correspondence or no modeling restrictions. The inspected v2 is later than the 2025 proceedings.
status: peer-reviewed conference proceedings; inspected arXiv revision

title: SCOT: Single-Cell Multi-Omics Alignment with Optimal Transport
training_information: Separate matrices; within-assay kNN graph distances; no feature or cell correspondences required.
objective: Entropically regularized GW coupling followed by barycentric projection.
target: Probabilistic cell correspondence and aligned measurements.
training_pairing: Unpaired core fit; self-tuning uses GW cost.
validation_information: Simulation truth and coassays; paper also compares correspondence-based parameter selection.
theorem_applicability: GW/OT optimization theory does not identify a biological residual coupling; observed-law counterexamples remain applicable.
positive_restrictions: Assumes shared biology expressed in sufficiently comparable geometry.
evidence_locator: §2.1–2.4; Algorithm 1; real-data evaluation.
caveat: Unsupervised self-tuning is a heuristic, not a causal-identification theorem.

title: SCOTv2: Single-Cell Multiomic Alignment with Disproportionate Cell-Type Representation
training_information: Separate assay geometry; anchor modality for multiple assays; no required cross-assay feature matches.
objective: Unbalanced GW relaxes mass constraints; barycentric mapping/coembedding.
target: Alignment with unequal cell-type proportions and multiple modalities.
training_pairing: Unpaired fit and self-tuning variant.
validation_information: Coassays and noncoassays with natural/simulated imbalance; cell labels assess accuracy.
theorem_applicability: Relaxing marginal mass constraints handles imbalance but does not observe cross-assay residual dependence.
positive_restrictions: Shared cell types/lineages and informative within-assay geometry.
evidence_locator: Introduction; §2 Methods; self-tuning and noncoassay evaluations.
caveat: Explicitly distinguishes noncoassay sampling from coassay benchmarks; retain that positive advance.

title: Manifold alignment for heterogeneous single-cell multi-omics data integration using Pamona
training_information: Within-assay geodesic distances and shared mass estimate; optional cell-type or cell-pair prior.
objective: Partial entropic GW with virtual cells, then geometry-preserving embedding.
target: Shared and assay-specific populations and probabilistic coupling.
training_pairing: Unpaired default; supervised extension supported.
validation_information: Simulations/coassays; heterogeneous PBMC analysis incorporates cell-type annotations.
theorem_applicability: Partial-transport construction is not a theorem identifying biological causal edges.
positive_restrictions: Comparable partial manifolds; known labels/pairs reduce alignment ambiguity.
evidence_locator: §2.1–2.2; §3.5; Discussion.
caveat: Best label-assisted examples cannot be treated as unsupervised evidence.

publication_dates.preferred_year_basis: journal issue year, matching publisher citation
publication_dates.note: Crossref online publication year 2021 and issue year 2022 are both correct; they identify the same article.

title: Unsupervised topological alignment for single-cell multi-omics integration
training_information: Separate feature matrices without cell or feature links; within-assay geodesic distances.
objective: Soft distance-matrix matching with global scale, then coupled t-SNE-like embedding.
target: Cell alignment and shared embedding.
training_pairing: Unpaired core; known matches can constrain the matching matrix.
validation_information: Simulations and coassayed sc-GEM/scNMT benchmarks.
theorem_applicability: Optimization claims concern matching; Discussion explicitly recognizes indistinguishable symmetric structures.
positive_restrictions: Similar intrinsic topology, sufficiently asymmetric informative geometry.
evidence_locator: Methods A1–A3; Discussion limitations.
caveat: Reported biological asymmetry can help alignment; it is not a general residual-copula identification condition.

title: Jointly Embedding Multiple Single-Cell Omics Measurements
training_information: Separate within-domain kernels; no known cell/feature correspondences.
objective: MMD between latent distributions plus distortion and projection penalties.
target: Shared manifold embedding.
training_pairing: Unpaired fitting.
validation_information: Synthetic manifolds and 61 coassayed methylation/expression cells.
theorem_applicability: Representer theorem supports kernel parameterization; no biological causal-identification theorem located in inspected methods.
positive_restrictions: Shared manifold and similar latent point distributions with enough structure to align.
evidence_locator: Methods: unsupervised manifold alignment, MMD-MA algorithm, optimization; Discussion.
caveat: Nonconvex optimization and matching ambiguity are distinct limitations.

title: Unsupervised manifold alignment for single-cell multi-omics data
training_information: Separate measurements; extends MMD-MA GPU implementation and bandwidth selection.
objective: Inherited MMD, distortion and projection objective.
target: Practical alignment of approximately 2,000-cell coassays.
training_pairing: Core alignment does not require correspondence.
validation_information: Coassayed RNA/accessibility datasets and parameter comparisons.
theorem_applicability: No causal-theorem conclusion drawn from abstract/limited indexed method excerpts.
positive_restrictions: Inherited shared-manifold premise; demonstrated practical scaling.
evidence_locator: Abstract and indexed §2.6–2.7 excerpts; original 2019 methods separately inspected.
caveat: Full-text browser blocked and Europe PMC XML failed; not a complete methods audit.

title: MATCHER: manifold alignment reveals correspondence between single cell transcriptome and epigenome dynamics
training_information: Separate matrices, biological orientation prior, same population/process/cell type.
objective: GPLVM pseudotime followed by monotone quantile warping to common master time.
target: State correspondence, generated profiles and cross-modal correlations.
training_pairing: Unpaired mode; separate paired shared-GPLVM extension.
validation_information: scM&T-seq/sc-GEM pairs withheld for validation; independent-lab RNA comparison.
theorem_applicability: Restricted monotone state completion can succeed; no unrestricted residual-coupling or causal-DAG identification follows.
positive_restrictions: One-dimensional monotone process; common sampling distribution; correct orientation supplied biologically.
evidence_locator: Overview assumptions; correlation evaluation; Methods warping; paired extension.
caveat: Paper explicitly says correct orientation cannot be inferred from data alone.

title: Bi-order multimodal integration of single-cell data
training_information: Unpaired matrices plus initial feature-conversion/fusion matrix, such as gene activity.
objective: Iterative cell- and feature-level CCA with regularization toward initial conversion.
target: Coembedding, fusion matrix, imputation and association networks.
training_pairing: No cell pairs required for fitting.
validation_information: Coassayed retina/bone marrow and predicted-profile correlations.
theorem_applicability: Fixed-point/local-convergence claim is computational, not causal identification.
positive_restrictions: Useful initial feature correspondence and shared correlated structure.
evidence_locator: Methods: initializing feature matching, Bi-CCA, parameter optimization, protein–gene networks.
caveat: Protein–gene networks use correlations in imputed profiles; no directed intervention claim established.

title: scDART: integrating unmatched scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data and learning cross-modality relationship simultaneously
training_information: Separate RNA/ATAC matrices and genomic gene-activity prior; optional root/cell anchors.
objective: Neural activity mapping, diffusion-distance preservation, MMD alignment and prior sparsity.
target: Integrated trajectories and nonlinear accessibility-to-expression mapping.
training_pairing: Unpaired core; scDART-anchor uses known correspondences.
validation_information: Unmatched datasets, coassays and simulated activity functions.
theorem_applicability: A learned regulatory mapping is model-dependent; no general causal-identification theorem located in inspected methods.
positive_restrictions: Similar trajectories; prior zeros assumed correct and prior ones may be false positives.
evidence_locator: Methods: prior GAM, trajectory preservation, MMD, anchors; Discussion.
caveat: Paper acknowledges imperfect prediction and recommends paired data for stronger prediction when available.

title: scJoint integrates atlas-scale single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data with transfer learning
training_information: Annotated RNA and unlabeled ATAC collections.
objective: Neural joint training of labeled/unlabeled observations; detailed losses not independently audited here.
target: Cell-type label transfer and joint visualization.
training_pairing: Cell pairs not required; RNA labels are supervision.
validation_information: Atlases, ASAP-seq and CITE-seq label accuracy.
theorem_applicability: No causal-identification conclusion drawn from abstract-only evidence.
positive_restrictions: Informative annotated reference and transferable cell identities.
evidence_locator: PubMed primary abstract and bibliographic record.
caveat: Original full-text retrieval blocked; cannot classify this as wholly unsupervised or claim a full objective audit.

title: sciCAN: single-cell chromatin accessibility and gene expression data integration via cycle-consistent adversarial network
training_information: Gene-aligned expression/accessibility inputs; augmented within-assay cells; no cell-type labels required.
objective: Noise-contrastive representation, modality adversary, generated-accessibility adversary and latent cycle loss.
target: Coembedding, label transfer, trajectories and activity–expression analyses.
training_pairing: Unpaired integration.
validation_information: Five datasets; Multiome hematopoietic hierarchy; CRISPR examples are downstream applications.
theorem_applicability: Cycle consistency constrains a chosen mapping; does not identify unrestricted biological residual coupling.
positive_restrictions: Comparable shared features and coherent latent mapping.
evidence_locator: Methods: Representation learning, Domain adaptation, Cycle-consistent network; Results.
caveat: Perturbation applications must not be treated as information available in our baseline.

title: scTopoGAN: unsupervised manifold alignment of single-cell data
training_information: Separate matrices, no overlapping cells/features or training labels required.
objective: Topology-preserving autoencoders; select GAN alignments by persistent-pairing distortion.
target: Cell-type/trajectory-aligned manifolds.
training_pairing: Unpaired fitting; labels evaluated afterward.
validation_information: PBMC, bone marrow, scGEM cell-type matching.
theorem_applicability: Topology preservation selects mappings; no general causal-identification theorem located in inspected methods.
positive_restrictions: Modalities share sufficiently similar manifold topology.
evidence_locator: §2.1.1–2.1.2; Discussion.
caveat: Authors explicitly acknowledge imperfect shared-manifold assumption and difficulty without linking ground truth.

title: SCIM: universal single-cell matching with unpaired feature sets
training_information: Separate matrices, no feature matches; censored cell labels orient the latent space.
objective: Reconstruction plus adversarial modality alignment; minimum-cost matching with null nodes.
target: Sibling-cell matching across technologies.
training_pairing: No physical cell pairs required; semisupervised label information used.
validation_information: Simulated pseudotime and real RNA/CyTOF cell-type concordance.
theorem_applicability: Paper explicitly gives reversed-trajectory alignment ambiguity; labels address orientation, not unrestricted residual causality.
positive_restrictions: Common low-dimensional structure, approximately shared population distribution and orientation supervision.
evidence_locator: §2.1 The orientation of latent space; §2.2; matching evaluation.
caveat: Reported matching accuracy is mainly cell-type agreement, not exact same-cell causal recovery.

title: MultiMAP: dimensionality reduction and integration of multimodal data
training_information: Full assay features plus shared-feature spaces/activity conversions; optional supplied correspondence in synthetic example.
objective: Construct multimodal fuzzy neighborhood graph and minimize embedding cross-entropy.
target: Integrated embedding/graph, clustering and trajectory comparisons.
training_pairing: Unpaired biological integration; synthetic Swiss-roll example supplies 1% manifold positions.
validation_information: Cell annotations, multiome pairing and structure metrics.
theorem_applicability: Riemannian/topological construction does not establish unrestricted causal-DAG identification.
positive_restrictions: Uniformity on a shared latent manifold and informative shared-feature neighborhoods.
evidence_locator: Methods MultiMAP; framework; synthetic-data description.
caveat: Using unshared features does not eliminate reliance on shared-feature information.

title: SCOT+: a comprehensive software suite for single-cell alignment using optimal transport
family: Unified GW, COOT and augmented GW transport
training_information: Separate matrices/geometry; optional known cell/feature supervision costs.
objective: Balanced/unbalanced cell and feature couplings with entropy and marginal penalties.
target: Cell/feature alignment and imputed coassay-like data.
training_pairing: Unsupervised and supervised configurations explicitly available.
validation_information: Balanced/imbalanced datasets and feature-supervised cross-species alignment.
theorem_applicability: Optimization formulations and feature couplings are not a causal-identification guarantee; observed-law argument applies to unsupervised modes.
positive_restrictions: Comparable geometry/features; reliable homolog or cell-label supervision improves specific matching.
evidence_locator: §2.1–2.4; §3.5; Discussion.
caveat: Discussion proposes future GRN applications; it does not establish that generated coassays retain causal truth.

title: BiCLUM: Bilateral contrastive learning for unpaired single-cell multi-omics integration
training_information: Gene activity or gene–protein correspondence; MNN pseudo-cell pairs and known feature pairs.
objective: Cell/feature autoencoder reconstruction plus bilateral InfoNCE.
target: Coembedding, label transfer and biological feature analyses.
training_pairing: No true cell pairs required; constructed MNN pairs train alignment.
validation_information: Paired and unpaired benchmarks, FOSCTTM and cell-type metrics.
theorem_applicability: Constructed positives are input-derived alignment choices, not observations of the missing residual joint.
positive_restrictions: Reliable converted features/MNN anchors and valid gene–protein mappings.
evidence_locator: Materials and methods, Steps 1–3; paired/unpaired benchmark sections.
caveat: PCA feeds encoders but MNNs use shared original feature space; distinguish both from biological pairing.

title: Integration of single-cell multi-omics data by regression analysis on unpaired observations
training_information: Unpaired RNA/ATAC covariance, genomic distances, cis support and initialization.
objective: Fit expression covariance with beta-transformed accessibility covariance; distance penalty and imputation refinement.
target: Cis-regulatory coefficients and predicted expression.
training_pairing: No paired observations required to fit.
validation_information: Simulations, multiome prediction and coembedding; some truth uses imputed data.
theorem_applicability: Positive restricted-model evidence; no coefficient-uniqueness/causal-identification theorem located in inspected methods.
positive_restrictions: Linear accessibility-to-expression model; conditionally independent gene errors; hard cis zeros beyond 200 kb.
evidence_locator: Methods UnpairReg model, Eqs.1–3; Algorithm; Discussion limitations.
caveat: Covariance factorization can be ambiguous; assumptions may fail for TF effects independent of accessibility.

title: Single-cell multi-omics integration for unpaired data by a siamese network with graph-based contrastive loss
training_information: Paired multiome/CITE-seq reference cells and cell-type labels; unpaired target inputs after training.
objective: Siamese true-pair contrastive loss, graph-based negative margins and cell-type classification.
target: Unpaired-target coembedding and smoothed mini-bulk regulatory associations.
training_pairing: Paired supervised training is required by the described model.
validation_information: Held-out datasets and pcHi-C support for inferred associations.
theorem_applicability: Outside the strict no-paired-reference baseline; cannot apply the same observed-law theorem without including training reference information.
positive_restrictions: Transferable paired labeled reference.
evidence_locator: Results overview; Methods Siamese network, margin, Training process.
caveat: Title's 'unpaired' describes target application, not the complete training information.

title: An interpretable Graph-Regularized Optimal Transport Framework for Diagonal Single-Cell Integrative Analysis
training_information: Within-assay kernels and kNN geometry; separate supervised/unsupervised benchmark settings.
objective: Latent Sinkhorn alignment, graph Laplacian smoothness and RKHS projection constraints.
target: Embedding, co-clustering and feature-importance/regulatory candidates.
training_pairing: Unsupervised mode exists; partial-label evaluation distinguished.
validation_information: Simulations and coassays; label transfer, FOSCTTM and biological enrichment.
theorem_applicability: Representer theorem concerns kernel representation, not identification of the biological joint or causal graph.
positive_restrictions: Shared manifold/lineage geometry; optional supervision; motif and proximity evidence for regulatory interpretation.
evidence_locator: Methods Problem formulation through GROTIA algorithm; interpretability; Results semi/unsupervised settings.
caveat: Embedding derivatives and motif/proximity-supported pairs are not intervention-effect estimates.

title: A unified computational framework for single-cell data integration with optimal transport
family: Coupled variational autoencoding and unbalanced optimal transport
training_information: Unpaired matrices with common and assay-specific variable genes; chromatin gene-activity conversion supplies feature correspondence.
objective: Coupled-VAE ELBO plus minibatch unbalanced OT between Gaussian latent posteriors.
target: Integrated cell embeddings, probabilistic transport and cross-dataset imputation.
training_pairing: Core RNA/ATAC study hides pairs; optional annotations, known correspondence and sample weights are supported.
validation_information: Paired PBMC pairs reserved for evaluation, unpaired RNA/ATAC benchmarks and held-out-gene spatial imputation.
theorem_applicability: Strict convexity of the fixed-cost regularized transport subproblem selects a plan; it does not identify biological residual coupling or a causal graph.
positive_restrictions: Informative shared genes/activity conversion and common latent measurement model; relaxed marginals accommodate unmatched populations.
evidence_locator: Methods: uniPort framework Eqs.1–7; Data preprocessing; Results: uniPort integrates scATAC and scRNA data; Discussion.
caveat: Positive paired-cell and imputation results are not a general direct-edge guarantee; activity construction influences results.

title: SIMBA: single-cell embedding along with features
training_information: Cell–feature relations and optional sequence/motif annotations; unpaired RNA/ATAC graphs linked by gene-activity-derived mutual neighbors after SVD.
objective: Typed negative-sampling graph-link prediction with dot-product scores, log loss and embedding regularization.
target: Cell/feature co-embedding, markers, modality integration and candidate regulatory relationships.
training_pairing: Supports unpaired integration and paired multimodal analysis as separate graph constructions.
validation_information: Unpaired integration tested by masking dual-omics pairing; main regulator/target demonstration uses paired SHARE-seq and motif/proximity evidence.
theorem_applicability: Graph-link likelihood is conditional on constructed edges; no general causal-identification theorem found in inspected methods.
positive_restrictions: Shared activity features, motif compatibility and genomic proximity constrain predictions; paired graphs contain extra joint information.
evidence_locator: Methods: Batch correction; Multi-omics integration; Graph embeddings with type constraints; Identification of TF target genes. Results: multimodal analysis versus multi-omics integration.
caveat: Do not attribute paired regulator evidence to the unpaired-only arm, or treat computational neighbor edges as observed cell pairing.

title: Comprehensive Integration of Single-Cell Data
training_information: Corresponding features, CCA/PCA and mutual-neighbor anchors. RNA/ATAC alignment uses gene-level accessibility summaries; reference-label transfer additionally uses reference labels. Protein transfer uses a CITE-seq reference with paired RNA/protein.
target: Dataset harmonization, cell-state annotation and transfer of measured features.
theorem_applicability: Mode-dependent: strictly disjoint anchor construction with only allowed feature mappings is covered; paired-reference feature transfer has additional joint information and is outside that contract.
positive_restrictions: Representative shared features and transferable reference neighborhoods support alignment/prediction; they do not identify arbitrary residual copulas.
evidence_locator: STAR Methods: dimensional reduction, anchor identification, data integration and label transfer; Results protein imputation.
caveat: Anchor pairs are inferred correspondences, not necessarily the same cell. Treat reference-assisted modes separately.
discovery_note: Nominated boundary method, verified by targeted primary-source lookup; not necessarily retrieved within the capped central OpenAlex queries.

title: Integrated analysis of multimodal single-cell data
training_information: Multiple modalities measured in the same cells. Within- and cross-modality neighbor prediction learns cell-specific modality weights; no cell-type labels are needed for those weights.
target: Joint cell representation, clustering, visualization and state definition.
theorem_applicability: Outside strict-disjoint setting in its native form: same-cell correspondence is an input.
positive_restrictions: Paired measurements provide joint observational evidence; downstream causal orientation still needs separate assumptions.
evidence_locator: STAR Methods: Weighted Nearest Neighbor Analysis; within/across-modality prediction and cell-specific weights.
caveat: A WNN cell-neighbor graph is not a regulatory graph. Unimodal query mapping uses an already constructed reference.

title: Dictionary learning for integrative, multimodal and scalable single-cell analysis
training_information: An additional multiomic dataset measures both modalities in the same cells. Its cells become dictionary atoms; unimodal datasets are reconstructed in those shared coordinates. Annotated references support label transfer.
target: Cross-modality reference mapping and scalable integration, including histone and methylation queries.
theorem_applicability: Outside strict-disjoint information contract: the paired bridge supplies cross-view information.
positive_restrictions: Coverage of relevant states and transferability between bridge/reference/query populations are needed for successful mapping.
evidence_locator: Publisher abstract; indexed primary Results and Figure 1 workflow. Supplemental mathematical methods not inspected.
caveat: Publication online in 2023, issue year 2024. PMC author title includes 'massively'. Publisher/PMC full-text access failed; source excerpts verify bridge requirement.

title: Single-Cell Multi-omic Integration Compares and Contrasts Features of Brain Cell Identity
training_information: Unpaired datasets on corresponding gene-level features. Integrative nonnegative factorization learns shared and dataset-specific metagenes; factor-neighborhood construction and normalization align cells. No true cell pairs required.
target: Shared/dataset-specific variation and cell identity across datasets/modalities.
theorem_applicability: Covered for independent disjoint assays with fixed allowed gene mappings and a broad causal class.
positive_restrictions: Common metagene structure and meaningful shared features can support state alignment; NMF constraints are not general causal restrictions.
evidence_locator: Figure 1; Methods: Performing iNMF Using Block Coordinate Descent, Equation 1.
caveat: This record concerns original LIGER, not later unshared-feature extensions. Regulatory-element nomination is not intervention identification.
discovery_note: Nominated boundary method, verified by targeted primary-source lookup; not necessarily retrieved within the capped central OpenAlex queries.

title: Multi-Omics Factor Analysis—a framework for unsupervised integration of multi-omics data sets
training_information: Multiple views measured on the same or partially overlapping identified samples. A common sample-factor matrix and view-specific loadings allow missing entries/views; feature identities need not match between views.
target: Major sources of variation, factor interpretation, clustering and missing-data imputation.
theorem_applicability: Native overlapping-sample use is outside strict-disjoint assumptions. Completely disconnected sample/view blocks require additional constraints; permitting missing values alone does not identify their joint.
positive_restrictions: A valid shared-factor model and enough linked observations support estimation of common factors.
evidence_locator: Results and Figure 1; Materials and Methods: model specification and missing values.
caveat: Shared factors and loadings describe variation, not directed causal effects. Original examples include bulk samples and paired single cells.
discovery_note: Nominated boundary method, verified by targeted primary-source lookup; not necessarily retrieved within the capped central OpenAlex queries.

title: MOFA+: a statistical framework for comprehensive integration of multi-modal single-cell data
training_information: Sample-indexed views plus known groups such as experiments/conditions. Shared view loadings and group-specific factor activities, sparse/ARD priors and missing-data handling extend MOFA. Different cell groups may be disjoint while modalities remain linked within observed samples.
target: Shared and group/view-specific variability, interpretable factors and scalable multimodal analysis.
theorem_applicability: Depends on observation pattern: paired/overlapping views are outside strict-disjoint contract. Disjoint experimental groups are not synonymous with unlinked modalities.
positive_restrictions: Connected observation patterns and correct factor/sparsity assumptions support joint estimation.
evidence_locator: Figure 1; Methods: model regularization and guidelines for groups/views.
caveat: Missing-view tolerance does not demonstrate identification for wholly disconnected modality blocks; no general regulatory-DAG theorem inferred.
discovery_note: Nominated boundary method, verified by targeted primary-source lookup; not necessarily retrieved within the capped central OpenAlex queries.

title: MultiVI: deep generative model for the integration of multimodal data
training_information: Jointly profiled RNA/ATAC cells plus optional RNA-only/ATAC-only cells and batch covariates. Modality encoders are aligned/averaged for paired observations, with observed-modality likelihoods and adversarial alignment. Additional protein modalities are supported.
target: Joint state representations, missing-modality imputation, uncertainty and differential analysis.
theorem_applicability: Published paired-assisted regime is outside strict-disjoint contract. A hypothetical all-disjoint, no-paired-pretraining mode remains subject to the theorem; the paper's 1–99% artificial unpairing is not proof for that setting.
positive_restrictions: Sufficient representative paired data and transportable decoder relationships can support prediction.
evidence_locator: Results: model, paired/unpaired integration; Methods: inference/training; official MultiVI model documentation.
caveat: Artificially unpaired cells appear in both assay lists; remaining cells are paired. This is not independent disjoint sampling. No all-unpaired guarantee claimed here.
discovery_note: Nominated boundary method, verified by targeted primary-source lookup; not necessarily retrieved within the capped central OpenAlex queries.

title: Joint probabilistic modeling of single-cell multi-omic data with totalVI
training_information: Same-cell RNA/protein counts from CITE-seq, with optional batch/donor covariates. Supports differing antibody panels and RNA-only batches in addition to jointly profiled training data.
target: Joint representation, protein-background correction, feature correlation estimation, integration and differential expression.
theorem_applicability: Outside strict-disjoint contract for its paired training regime, including subsequent unimodal queries.
positive_restrictions: Paired observation and appropriate count/background/batch models support estimating joint observational relationships.
evidence_locator: Results: The totalVI model; Methods: conditional joint distribution p(x_n,y_n|s_n), integration with missing proteins.
caveat: Useful explicit counterexample to 'integration never recovers relationships': paired-data correlation estimation is a stated task, but correlation is not causal orientation.

title: Cobolt: integrative analysis of multimodal single-cell sequencing data
training_information: Joint-modality cells provide the linkage between distinct feature spaces; optional separate RNA-only and ATAC-only datasets are integrated through the multimodal latent model and transfer correction. No peak-to-gene matching is required.
target: Shared cell representation, joint clustering and integration of multimodal/unimodal datasets.
theorem_applicability: Outside strict-disjoint contract in the demonstrated integration setup: jointly sequenced bridge cells are supplied.
positive_restrictions: Representative paired cells and transferable latent factors permit cross-view estimation.
evidence_locator: Results: The Cobolt model; Methods: hierarchical model and correcting missing modalities.
caveat: A missing-modality encoder is not evidence that training with no paired bridge identifies the same joint.

title: A deep generative model for multi-view profiling of single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data
training_information: RNA counts and TF-IDF-transformed ATAC profiles from the same cells. Joint encoder/decoder with Gaussian-mixture latent prior, attention modules and clustering-consistency constraints. The mixture component is inferred, not automatically an observed cell-type label.
target: Joint embedding, denoising/imputation, clustering, trajectories and cis-regulatory-element analysis.
theorem_applicability: Outside strict-disjoint contract: the joint observations and matched rows are inputs.
positive_restrictions: Same-cell data allow joint observational estimation subject to model/noise adequacy.
evidence_locator: Results: The scMVP model, Figure 1 and joint ELBO; Methods: multi-view model.
caveat: CRE identification and inferred cluster consistency do not alone establish direct causal direction. Do not describe this as an unpaired-only algorithm.
discovery_note: Nominated boundary method, verified by targeted primary-source lookup; not necessarily retrieved within the capped central OpenAlex queries.

title: A mixture-of-experts deep generative model for integrated analysis of single-cell multiomics data
training_information: Paired multimodal training observations. Each modality's encoder learns latent values that reconstruct all measured modalities through a mixture-of-experts posterior; trained encoders support unimodal cross-generation.
target: Interpretable latent representation, clustering and bidirectional missing-modality generation.
theorem_applicability: Outside strict-disjoint contract when trained as published on paired CITE-seq/SHARE-seq cells.
positive_restrictions: Learnable cross-view relationships and training coverage can support prediction on related cells.
evidence_locator: Figure 1; STAR Methods: ELBO for x_1:M and mixture-of-experts; training/test split descriptions.
caveat: Decoder traversals called regulatory programs are model feature associations; generating an unobserved modality does not identify intervention effects.
discovery_note: Nominated boundary method, verified by targeted primary-source lookup; not necessarily retrieved within the capped central OpenAlex queries.

title: BABEL enables cross-modality translation between multiomic profiles at single-cell resolution
training_information: Jointly profiled RNA/ATAC cells train interoperable modality encoders and decoders using within- and cross-modality reconstruction. Trained networks are applied to single-modality cells; additional protein translation is demonstrated.
target: Cross-modality prediction and hypothesis generation in related cell contexts.
theorem_applicability: Outside strict-disjoint contract: paired training supervision contributes joint information even when deployment queries are unimodal.
positive_restrictions: Transferability from sufficiently representative paired training examples and adequate predictive model.
evidence_locator: Results: design/training on jointly profiled cells; Methods: model architecture and training.
caveat: Cross-decoding predicts outcomes; it does not implement a biological intervention. Performance on new contexts does not remove distribution-shift assumptions.

title: Cross-Linked Unified Embedding for cross-modality representation learning
training_information: Partially paired multimodal cells supervise self/cross encoders into modality-specific subspaces. Self/cross ELBOs, same-cell representation agreement and adversarial alignment enable missing-modality embeddings.
target: Comprehensive embeddings, cross-modality matching and prediction.
theorem_applicability: Outside strict-disjoint contract in its published supervised regime; true paired training is explicit.
positive_restrictions: Paired coverage and transferable cross-encoder mappings support correspondence estimation.
evidence_locator: NeurIPS paper Sections 3, 4.3–4.5; Introduction explicitly states paired multimodal supervision.
caveat: CLUE is distinct from unsupervised GLUE despite sharing a software package. Challenge matching accuracy is not causal-DAG identification.
discovery_note: Nominated boundary method, verified by targeted primary-source lookup; not necessarily retrieved within the capped central OpenAlex queries.

title: Joint variational autoencoders for multimodal imputation and embedding
training_information: Two modality matrices and optional user correspondence F, including known same-cell pairs. Joint VAEs aggregate corresponding latent values. Additional inferred correspondence is derived from within-assay geodesic distances; reconstruction, KL, combination and alignment losses are used.
target: Cross-modal embedding, phenotype prediction, imputation and feature attribution.
theorem_applicability: Known-pair F lies outside strict-disjoint contract. With only data-derived correspondence and independent disjoint cells, the theorem applies to general causal recovery.
positive_restrictions: True correspondence or a valid restrictive manifold/coupling assumption can improve recoverability.
evidence_locator: Methods 4.1, 4.6–4.8; Equation 8 inferred correspondence; Figure 2.
caveat: SHAP feature importance is predictive, not an intervention effect. The paper primarily evaluates partial known correspondence; do not silently treat inferred F as observed pairs.
discovery_note: Nominated boundary method, verified by targeted primary-source lookup; not necessarily retrieved within the capped central OpenAlex queries.

title: Fast, sensitive and accurate integration of single-cell data with Harmony
training_information: A common low-dimensional feature embedding, normally PCA of shared expression features, and known batch/covariate labels. Soft diversity-aware clustering and local linear correction; spatial-expression example uses shared genes.
target: Batch-adjusted embedding preserving cell-state variation.
theorem_applicability: Primarily horizontal/common-feature comparator, not an estimator of a missing cross-assay joint. If repurposed on disjoint assays, derived corrections do not escape the theorem.
positive_restrictions: Adequate common representation and separable batch/biological effects support harmonization.
evidence_locator: Online Methods 1.1 and 1.4; Discussion: corrected coordinates and original expression retained.
caveat: Do not classify horizontal batch correction as failed cross-assay causal recovery. Optional labels/initial clusters must be disclosed.
discovery_note: Nominated boundary method, verified by targeted primary-source lookup; not necessarily retrieved within the capped central OpenAlex queries.

title: Paired single-cell multi-omics data integration with Mowgli
training_information: Every omics matrix has the same identified cell columns. Shared nonnegative cell factors and modality-specific loadings minimize entropic OT reconstruction plus entropy regularization; feature costs use within-modality cosine distances. No cell-type labels are required for the factorization.
target: Joint cell embedding, clustering and interpretable feature programs.
theorem_applicability: Outside the strict-disjoint contract: observed same-cell correspondence links the modalities.
positive_restrictions: Pairing provides joint information; low-dimensional nonnegative factors impose a representation model.
evidence_locator: Results: Mowgli a new tool, Eq. 1; Methods: Notations, Optimal transport, Mowgli; same cell columns and within-modality ground costs.
caveat: OT is a reconstruction loss here, not evidence that OT can identify arbitrary missing cell couplings or orient causal edges.

title: scMoMaT jointly performs single cell mosaic integration and multi-modal bio-marker detection
training_information: Shared cell-batch or feature entities connect observed matrices. If disconnected, annotation-derived pseudo-modalities connect them: binarized gene-body/upstream-2kb ATAC sums become pseudo-RNA; corresponding RNA counts become pseudo-protein. Matrix tri-factorization shares cell/feature factors and association components; clusters are inferred, then used for marker retraining.
target: Mosaic cell integration, clustering and cluster-specific multimodal biomarkers.
theorem_applicability: Mode-dependent: observed paired bridges add joint information; pseudo-modalities computed from strict-disjoint assays plus fixed annotation remain within the theorem.
positive_restrictions: Connected entity graph and shared low-rank factors support integration; generated feature proxies encode assumptions about modality correspondence.
evidence_locator: Framework Eqs. 1–3 and entity connectivity; Methods: Calculating pseudo-count matrices, Retraining procedure.
caveat: Pseudo-RNA is not a second measured assay. Marker importance and association matrices do not by themselves establish direct regulation.

title: Old and new approaches in statistical matching when samples are drawn with complex survey designs
publication_status: Istat-hosted author manuscript; publication year and venue not established from inspected copy
observation_contract: Distinct independent samples observe (X,Y) and (X,Z) from a common population.
target: Joint relationships among never-coobserved variables; identified sets rather than only sampling uncertainty.
assumptions: General block marginals do not determine the joint. Conditional independence or auxiliary restrictions can select a completion; complex survey designs require separate sampling treatment.
theorem_applicability: Direct context for the missing residual-coupling problem. Supports model-class-qualified nonidentification, not universal failure of restricted models.
evidence_locator: Author manuscript pp.1–2; §3 equations (5)–(6) define compatible joint distributions.
discovery_origin: prior focused review; direct primary retrieval

title: Unlinked Monotone Regression
observation_contract: Separate predictor and response samples; unlike shuffled regression they need not contain the same individuals or sample sizes.
target: A scalar monotone regression function, not an unrestricted multivariate causal DAG.
assumptions: Independent additive structural noise with known distribution; monotonicity; stated design/deconvolution regularity. Unknown-noise extensions use additional information.
theorem_applicability: Genuine recovery from unpaired marginals within a restricted model class. Known count-measurement noise does not automatically supply the required biological structural-noise law.
evidence_locator: Introduction pp.3–4; Assumption A0 §2.2; Theorems 1–5; §7 unknown-noise extensions.
discovery_origin: prior focused review; direct primary retrieval

title: Challenging Common Assumptions in the Unsupervised Learning of Disentangled Representations
observation_contract: Unsupervised observations from an unrestricted latent generative model; no informative auxiliary supervision.
target: Recovery of disentangled latent coordinates.
assumptions: Dimension greater than one and a factorized latent density; the model class admits entangling bijections with identical observable distributions.
theorem_applicability: Related information argument, but not a theorem about original measured-variable DAGs or every structured multimodal model. Correct inductive restrictions can exclude alternatives.
evidence_locator: §3, Theorem 1 and following construction; Appendix A.

title: Nonlinear ICA Using Auxiliary Variables and Generalized Contrastive Learning
observation_contract: Each observed mixture accompanies an auxiliary variable such as time, history, or treatment label.
target: Latent components up to componentwise transformations; some exponential-family cases retain linear ambiguity.
assumptions: Conditional source independence, invertible smooth mixing/demixing, sufficiently diverse auxiliary modulation, and specified contrastive regression class.
theorem_applicability: Auxiliary information can identify sources under restrictions. An arbitrary integrated state or label does not automatically satisfy variability or independence, and sources are not a causal DAG.
evidence_locator: §4 Theorems 1–3; §5 warns against arbitrary auxiliary-variable construction.

title: Variational Autoencoders and Nonlinear ICA: A Unifying Framework
observation_contract: An observed mixture and auxiliary covariate are jointly available per sample.
target: Latent generative model/posterior equivalence class, not arbitrary original cross-assay causal edges.
assumptions: Injective mixing; conditionally factorized exponential-family latents; fixed observation-noise model with the characteristic-function condition; full-rank auxiliary modulation. Stronger equivalence needs further conditions.
theorem_applicability: A positive restricted identification result. Basic Theorem 1 permits linear sufficient-statistic ambiguity; ordinary multimodal VAEs do not inherit it merely by using a shared latent space.
evidence_locator: §4 Theorems 1–4; Proposition 1 covers unresolved Gaussian location-modulation ambiguity.

title: The Incomplete Rosetta Stone problem: Identifiability results for Multi-view Nonlinear ICA
publication_status: UAI 2019 proceedings published as PMLR 115:217–227 in 2020
observation_contract: Simultaneous views of the same source realization; contrastive learning distinguishes genuine joint tuples from shuffled tuples.
target: Shared independent sources or their corrupted versions, up to stated transformations.
assumptions: Invertible view mixing, componentwise independent corruption and sufficiently distinct views; noiseless/noisy/many-view results differ.
theorem_applicability: The true joint-view information differs from disjoint assay marginals. It cannot justify treating integration-generated pairs as observed positive pairs.
evidence_locator: §3 model equations (5)–(7), Theorems 1, 4, 5 and 8; §2 contrastive sampling.
discovery_origin: known primary source and central OpenAlex query06

title: Statistical Matching via Schrödinger Bridge beyond Conditional Independence
observation_contract: Partially overlapping (X,Y) and (X,Z) samples; reported tuning can additionally use complete auxiliary triplets.
target: Joint-distribution recovery and predictive completion, not causal orientation.
assumptions: Gaussian recovery theorem requires an oracle cost or residual-sign-compatible alignment cost and a suitable regularization parameter.

evidence_locator: Theorem 3.2; §3.2 tuning discussion; Appendix A parameter formula and B.4 auxiliary-triplet validation.

title: Unpaired Multi-Domain Causal Representation Learning
observation_contract: Only separate domain marginals; no paired measurements or interventions required by the theorem.
target: The observed joint law is identified exactly; signed-block representation ambiguities leave that law invariant. The shared latent DAG is identified up to relabeling; its coefficients can retain sign ambiguities.
assumptions: Linear latent SEM and full-column-rank linear views, with no unspecified extra count kernel; independent distinct nonsymmetric standardized errors. Graph recovery needs separated shared/private blocks, two partial pure children per shared latent and rank faithfulness.
theorem_applicability: A genuine counterexample to blanket impossibility from unpaired data. Its restricted model excludes the Gaussian counterfamily; it does not establish arbitrary feature-level regulation from raw counts.
evidence_locator: Official PDF: Eq. (1)–(2) and Definition 2.1, pp4–5; C1–C2 and Theorem 3.1, p6; Definition 4.2 and C3–C4, pp7–8; Theorem 4.4, p8; Remark 3.3 and Appendix C.
discovery_origin: central OpenAlex query05 and supplementary primary search
measurement_scope: Domain-private latent factors can represent noise within this model; appending Poisson/negative-binomial observations is not licensed by the theorem without another identification argument.
joint_graph_scope_distinction: Remark 3.3 permits shared-to-private directed paths for joint-law identification, but no private-to-shared paths. Section 4 uses separated shared/private blocks for its shared-graph identification theorem.

title: Identifiable Shared Component Analysis of Unpaired Multimodal Mixtures
observation_contract: Unpaired linear mixtures of common and private components; separate variants add identical mixing structure or a few paired anchors.
target: Aligned shared components up to a common invertible linear transform; stronger ICA variants recover individual components.
assumptions: Full-column-rank mixing, full-rank shared covariance, modality variability and restrictions removing distribution-preserving ambiguities; anchor variants have different assumptions.
theorem_applicability: Unpaired distribution matching can be identifiable within restricted models. The shared-subspace result is not a theorem identifying arbitrary residual couplings or a causal DAG.
evidence_locator: Official PDF: Eq. (1), §2; Assumption 1 and Theorem 1, pp4–5; Corollary 1, p5; additional same-mixing and paired-anchor variants in §4, pp6–7; Appendix H private components.
discovery_origin: central OpenAlex query06 and supplementary primary search

title: Propensity Score Alignment of Unpaired Multimodal Data
publication_status: NeurIPS 37 (2024), main conference; official proceedings verified
observation_contract: Separate modalities with observed experimental labels perturbing a shared latent state.
target: A common identifiable propensity representation and matching/prediction, not a causal DAG.
